observation.visible_scene: A shallow-focus outdoor scene: a soft green-and-white bokeh background with several yellow daisy-like flowers in the lower portion, including a prominent orange flower (right-of-center) on which a small dark insect sits throughout. A butterfly with black-and-white spotted wings edged in orange-brown is the main moving subject.
visible_changes: Frames 1-10: the butterfly is airborne in the upper-left/center region, wings repeatedly spread and folded (flapping), drifting leftward and downward relative to the flowers.
Frames 11-20: the butterfly descends toward the lower-left yellow flower, its wings showing open and edge-on (closed) poses as it settles near that bloom.

Frames 21-41: the butterfly remains perched on the lower-left yellow flower, rhythmically opening and closing its wings (from fully spread to nearly vertical/edge-on) in a basking or fluttering motion; the small dark insect on the orange flower stays put.

Across the sequence the left yellow flower and the perched butterfly gradually shift toward the center of the frame while the orange flower moves toward the right edge, indicating a slow camera pan/zoom relative to the static flowers.
outside_clip_unknowns: What preceded the airborne hovering at the start, and whether the butterfly ultimately takes off again after the last frame.
The cause of the camera framing change (pan vs. zoom vs. tracking) is not determinable from the blurred background.
uncertain_details: Exact direction and nature of camera movement (the background is too blurred to confirm pan versus zoom).
Whether the early leftward/downward drift is the butterfly's own flight or partly camera framing; the relative position to the flowers does change, so at least some butterfly motion is real.
The identity of the small dark insect on the orange flower (out of focus).
